background.task:
All seven acceptance criteria in **SKILL.md §4a — Choosing an Extraction Method** were completed successfully against MockSite (`http://localhost:18080`), using only `browser4-cli` commands:

| AC | Branch | Command used | Result |
|----|--------|--------------|--------|
| AC1 | Interact first, then extract | `snapshot -i` → `fill`/`select`/`check` → `click` → `htmlsnapshot` → `htmlsnapshot get text "#result-data"` | ✅ Confirmation banner + submitted JSON (Jane / Smith / jane.smith@example.com / us / advanced) extracted and matched inputs |
| AC2 | Static, one field | `htmlsnapshot get text "#productTitle"` | ✅ `4K OLED TV 55` |
| AC3 | Static, all matches | `htmlsnapshot get all text '[class*="product-title"]'` | ✅ All 6 Electronics titles |
| AC4 | Correlated multi-field rows | `htmlsnapshot query --sql @ac4-final.sql` | ✅ 6 rows, title/price/URL aligned per card |
| AC5 | Dynamic/complex logic | `eval --json --file ac5-eval.js` | ✅ title, 2 buttons, 0 links, 0 forms, 5 headings |
| AC6 | Natural-language extraction | `extract "…" --stdout` | ✅ title / $199.99 / 4.4 / 2 feature bullets (backend has LLM key) |
| AC7 | High-volume bulk | `crawl --seed-file … --depth 0 --sql @… --format table --refresh` | ✅ 4 rows, one per seed URL |

**Important AC6 note:** The task said to record AC6 as *environment-blocked* if no LLM key was configured. My shell has no LLM key (all four env vars unset), but `extract` **succeeded** — `browser4-cli doctor` reports "✓ LLM is configured" on the **backend server** (port 18182). So the LLM key lives on the backend, not the CLI shell. This surfaced a documentation ambiguity (see Issue 10).

issues.title: SKILL.md §4a/§5 falsely claim htmlsnapshot is stale after JS interactions — it actually reflects the live DOM

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Fill+submit the client-side form-filling page, then: browser4-cli htmlsnapshot; browser4-cli htmlsnapshot get text "#result-data". It returns the just-submitted JSON payload, not the initial 'No submission yet.'

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Behavior should match the documentation. §5 states 'htmlsnapshot captures the initial page HTML, not the live DOM… the snapshot will be stale' and §4a says JS-modified content 'will not be reflected'.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: htmlsnapshot capture reflects the current live DOM: after a JS-driven form submission, get text "#result-data" returns the submitted values. The documented 'use eval instead' advice is therefore wrong for this version and would push users to a needlessly indirect path (and the reverse concern — trusting a genuinely-stale cached snapshot — is real and unaddressed).

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The docs describe an older implementation ('initial server-rendered HTML') while the current htmlsnapshot capture re-serializes the live DOM. The documentation was not updated when the capture semantics changed.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: skills/browser4-cli/SKILL.md lines 299 and 470-471 (and references/htmlsnapshot.md 'initial page HTML' wording)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Correct §4a/§5 to state that htmlsnapshot capture serializes the current live DOM and will reflect JS updates as long as you re-capture after interacting
- Clarify the real staleness rule: the *cached* snapshot is stale only if you do not re-capture after a navigation/interaction; document that the auto-captured snapshot after goto is a distinct earlier capture
- Add an explicit note in AC1-style scenarios: after submit, run htmlsnapshot (capture) before get, then eval is not required

issues.title: First goto reports "Page loaded" but the DOM is empty and stuck in readyState "loading"

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
browser4-cli goto "http://localhost:18080/generated/form-filling.html"
Then immediately: browser4-cli eval "document.readyState"  → returns "loading"; eval "document.querySelectorAll('input').length" → 0. The goto output printed "Page loaded" and even "wait --load networkidle" reported "✓ Wait complete".

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: After goto reports success, the page should be fully loaded (readyState "complete", populated DOM).

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The first navigation (reconnecting an existing DEFAULT session that was on /ec/dp/B0E000003) left the target URL set but the document empty: document.title was "", document.documentElement.outerHTML.length was null, and there were 0 inputs/selects/buttons. A second goto (which printed "Already at … page unchanged") actually completed the load (readyState "complete", 13 inputs).

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Likely a race in the reconnect-and-navigate path: when goto reuses a pre-existing session and navigates, the 'Page loaded' signal fires before the document finishes parsing/committing. The auto-captured snapshot and page-info read an empty document. Needs investigation into the goto navigation-completion detection (vs. the load-event/readyState it actually waits on).

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/main.rs (goto/navigation completion handling) — follow-up analysis needed

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Make goto's 'Page loaded' wait on document.readyState === 'complete' (or DOM content readiness), not just the HTTP navigation commit, before printing success and capturing the snapshot
- If the navigation is to the same URL the session already had, force a reload instead of printing 'page unchanged' with a stale empty DOM
- Surface a clearer diagnostic when the post-goto snapshot is empty (e.g. 'page appears empty; try wait --load networkidle or reload')

issues.title: CLI pollutes the repo root with 128 files across two inconsistently-named state directories

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run several browser4-cli commands from the repo root with an unwritable ~/.browser4. Observe D:\workspace\Browser4\Browser4-4.13\.browser4-cli\snapshot\ (128 files: snapshot-*.yml, extract-*.txt) and .\.browser4-cli-state\ (sessions\, loops\).

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: State/snapshots land in a single, clearly-named, configurable directory (ideally outside the repo, or at least consistently named and documented).

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Two sibling dirs are created at the repo root: .browser4-cli (snapshots/extract results, 128 files) and .browser4-cli-state (session/loop state). The warning text names .browser4-cli-state, but snapshots go to .browser4-cli, so a user cannot tell which env var controls which directory.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The CLI state fallback path and the snapshot-output path are computed independently and use different names ('.browser4-cli' vs '.browser4-cli-state'). BROWSER4_CLI_STATE_DIR relocates state but snapshots appear to be written to a separately-derived '.browser4-cli' path.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ (state-dir fallback and snapshot-dir resolution)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Unify snapshot and session state under one root (e.g. honor BROWSER4_CLI_STATE_DIR for both, defaulting snapshots under <state>/snapshot)
- Document the exact directory each artifact type is written to and the env var that controls it
- Prefer ~/.browser4 (outside the repo) when writable, and when falling back, print the full resolved path once rather than per-command

issues.title: PowerShell treats unquoted @file as a splat; documented `--sql @query.sql` fails on Windows

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
browser4-cli htmlsnapshot query "http://localhost:18080/ec/b?node=1292115012" --sql @.test-sessions/ac4-query.sql
→ ParserError: Unrecognized token in source text (the @ is the PowerShell splat operator).

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The @file syntax shown throughout SKILL.md/help should work in PowerShell (the primary Windows shell) or be documented with a Windows-safe form.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Unquoted @file is a PowerShell parse error. Quoting it (--sql "@.test-sessions/...") works, but the docs and help examples use the unquoted form copied from bash.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: @ is PowerShell's splat operator, so an unquoted @path token never reaches the CLI. The docs were written bash-first.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: skills/browser4-cli/SKILL.md (X-SQL quickstart examples) and references/htmlsnapshot.md / x-sql.md

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Add explicit PowerShell examples showing --sql "@query.sql" (quoted) alongside the bash form
- Add a note in the SKILL.md §4e and §5 shell-quoting warning that on PowerShell @file must be quoted

issues.title: PowerShell backslash-quote escaping breaks CSS selectors; must use single quotes

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
browser4-cli htmlsnapshot get all text "[class*=\"product-title\"]"
→ 'No elements matched "[class*=\".'

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: A clear, working way to pass a CSS attribute selector like [class*="x"] from PowerShell.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Using \" inside a double-quoted PowerShell string passes a mangled selector (the CLI sees '[class*="' truncated). Single quotes — '[class*="product-title"]' — work, but this is easy to get wrong and the error message is confusing (it echoes the truncated selector and suggests a nonsense command).

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: PowerShell uses the backtick for escaping, not backslash; \" is a literal backslash+quote. The docs' Windows guidance exists in shell-quoting.md but the primary SKILL.md examples use bash quoting.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: skills/browser4-cli/references/shell-quoting.md and SKILL.md §5 Critical Warnings

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Prominently document the single-quote pattern for PowerShell selectors with double-quoted attribute values
- Improve the empty-match error message to not echo a half-parsed selector and to drop the misleading 'query the live accessibility tree' suggestion

issues.title: DOM_FIRST_HREF(DOM, '.product-link') returns empty; requires tag-qualified selector or DOM_FIRST_ATTR

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
SELECT DOM_FIRST_HREF(DOM, '.product-link') AS link FROM DOM_LOAD_AND_SELECT(@url, '[class*="product-card"]')
→ link is "" for all rows. DOM_FIRST_HREF(DOM, 'a.product-link') → correct absolute URL; DOM_FIRST_ATTR(DOM, '.product-link', 'href') → correct relative URL.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: DOM_FIRST_HREF with any selector that matches an <a> element should return its href consistently.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: A class-only selector (.product-link) yields empty; the same element selected with a tag+class selector (a.product-link) works. The task's own AC4 instruction to use DOM_FIRST_HREF is a trap for a user who naturally writes the class-only selector.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: DOM_FIRST_HREF resolves relative→absolute and, per docs/ql-functions-guide.md:902-906, can return empty in scoped DOM. Empirically it is selector-sensitive (class-only fails, tag-qualified succeeds), which points to the internal element-selection vs. href-resolution step, not merely a base-URL absence. The function lives in an external Pulsar library (not this repo's .kt files).

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Investigate why firstHref(dom, '.product-link') and firstHref(dom, 'a.product-link') diverge for the same element, and normalize them
- Add a regression test for class-only vs tag-qualified selectors with relative hrefs in scoped DOM
- Update SKILL.md §4e/x-sql.md to call out this gotcha and recommend DOM_FIRST_ATTR for href extraction

issues.title: crawl.md MockSite selector table is inaccurate (#feature-bullets and .breadcrumb don't exist)

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Open http://localhost:18080/ec/dp/B0E000002 and inspect. crawl.md lists MockSite selectors: Description=#feature-bullets, Category=.breadcrumb. Neither selector matches (the actual IDs/classes are #product-features and .breadcrumbs).

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The documented MockSite selectors should match the served pages.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: #feature-bullets matches 0 elements; the feature list is <ul id="product-features">. The breadcrumb is .breadcrumbs (plural). Title (#productTitle) and price (#product-price) are correct.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The crawl.md selector table was written against a different/older template or the Amazon fixture, and was not reconciled with the current HtmlRenderer product template (ec-product.html) which uses #product-features and .breadcrumbs.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: skills/browser4-cli/references/crawl.md lines 272-280

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Correct the table to #productTitle, #product-price, #product-features, .breadcrumbs (and note the listing-page selectors .product-card/.product-title/.product-price)
- Add a note that listing pages use .product-title/.product-price classes while detail pages use #productTitle/#product-price IDs

issues.title: extract output is a Java-serialization wrapper with double-encoded JSON and leaked token metadata

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body:
browser4-cli extract "Return the product title, displayed price, rating, and the top three feature bullets as JSON." --stdout
→ {"type":"ai.platon.pulsar.agentic.ExtractResult","description":"{\"product_title\":…,\"metadata\":{…},\"inputToken\":1932,\"outputToken\":4872,\"totalToken\":6804,\"inferenceTimeMillis\":5}"}

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The user asked for '…as JSON'; they should get a clean JSON object (e.g. {"product_title":…,"displayed_price":…,"rating":…,"feature_bullets":[…]}) — not an implementation wrapper.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The requested data is correct but is (1) wrapped in a {"type","description"} envelope, (2) double-encoded as an escaped string inside 'description', (3) polluted with inputToken/outputToken/totalToken/inferenceTimeMillis and a metadata.completed:false field, and (4) saved to a file by default instead of stdout.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: MCPToolController.kt:952-959 has an 'is ExtractResult' branch that would emit clean {success,message,data} JSON, but the extract result apparently falls through to the generic else branch (lines 963-968) that wraps any non-serializable object as {type, description}. The token-usage stats are also merged into the result data node before serialization.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: browser4-rest/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/rest/mcp/controller/MCPToolController.kt:952-968 and browser4-agentic/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/agentic/PerceptiveAgent.kt:111-119

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Ensure the extract tool result is typed as ExtractResult at the serialization point so it hits the clean {success,message,data} branch
- Emit the LLM's structured data as the top-level payload and move token usage/inference timing into a separate, clearly-labeled metadata field (or strip it from user output)
- Default extract to --stdout for a single-page sync extraction, or clearly print the extracted JSON inline alongside the saved file path

issues.title: Permission-denied CLI-state warning printed on every single command

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: browser4-cli fill e1822 "Jane" (or any command) in a sandbox where C:\Users\<user>\.browser4 is not writable.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The fallback warning should appear once (or be suppressible), not on every command.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Every command prints two lines: 'cannot write CLI state to C:\Users\pereg\.browser4 (permission denied)' and 'using …\.browser4-cli-state instead — set BROWSER4_CLI_STATE_DIR to a writable location to silence this warning'. This adds noise to every interaction and clutters output that is otherwise meant to be parseable.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: The fallback/warning logic runs on each invocation with no deduplication or sticky suppression.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ (state-dir initialization/fallback warning)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Emit the warning only once per process lifetime (or cache a 'warned' marker)
- Add a --quiet-aware suppression or a dedicated config flag to silence it

issues.title: extract/agent help says the LLM key is 'configured in the environment' but the key lives on the backend server

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: Run browser4-cli extract … with no OPENROUTER_API_KEY/DEEPSEEK_API_KEY in the CLI shell. It succeeds; browser4-cli doctor shows '✓ LLM is configured'.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: The docs should specify where the LLM key must be set (the process/environment that runs the backend server, not the CLI shell).

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: extract worked because the separately-managed backend (port 18182) has the key. A first-time user who starts the backend themselves via the CLI would reasonably assume 'the environment' means their own shell; the reference (agent.md §Prerequisites) likewise shows export DEEPSEEK_API_KEY=… without stating it must reach the backend process.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Ambiguous phrasing — 'environment' can mean the CLI shell or the backend server environment. The architecture (CLI → REST backend → LLM) means the key must be visible to the backend JVM.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: skills/browser4-cli/references/agent.md (Prerequisites section) and cli/browser4-cli/src/help.rs (extract/chat help text)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Reword to: 'the key must be set in the environment of the Browser4 backend server process (wherever it runs); when the CLI auto-starts the backend, set it in the CLI's own environment before the first launch'
- Add a doctor-based tip ('LLM is configured/not configured') pointing users at the right place

issues.title: MockSite serves two different HTML structures for the same URL depending on Accept header

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: GET http://localhost:18080/ec/b?node=1292115012 with Accept */* (e.g. PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest) → article.product-card with h2.product-title. Same URL in browser4-cli (browser goto and scrape API) → div.product-card with div.product-title.

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: One stable markup for a given URL regardless of client Accept header, so selector discovery is unambiguous.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: Two Spring controllers map /ec/b (EcommerceController vs EcCategoryController); the more specific produces=text/html match wins for the browser, so browser4-cli consistently sees div.product-card, but a curl/Invoke-WebRequest with */* sees article.product-card. The fixture README's 'Suggested ID / Class Conventions' still documents article.product-card.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: MockSite fixture design: duplicated /ec/b mappings with different renderers and no unambiguous single winner across Accept values. Not a browser4-cli defect, but it undermines the scenario's selector discoverability when users cross-check with a different HTTP client.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: browser4-tests/pulsar-tests-common/src/main/kotlin/ai/platon/pulsar/test/server/ec/EcControllers.kt and EcommerceController.kt (duplicate /ec/b mappings)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Consolidate to a single /ec/b handler (or make both renderers emit the same product-card element tag/classes)
- Update the ec/README.md conventions to match the markup actually served to text/html clients (div.product-card / div.product-title)

issues.title: Misleading empty-match hint suggests htmlsnapshot get text queries 'the live accessibility tree'

sections.label: Reproduction
sections.body: browser4-cli htmlsnapshot get all text "[class*=\"product-title\"]" (with a mangled/empty selector) → 'No elements matched … Alternatively, use get text "…" to query the live accessibility tree instead of the stored snapshot.'

sections.label: Expected Behavior
sections.body: Accurate guidance: get/get all query the stored HTML snapshot via CSS selectors, not the accessibility tree.

sections.label: Actual Behavior
sections.body: The hint claims get text queries the live accessibility tree, which is incorrect (that is snapshot/eval territory). Combined with echoing the half-parsed selector, the recovery message actively misleads.

sections.label: Root Cause Analysis
sections.body: Copy/pasted or outdated hint text in the empty-result path; the selector truncation is a downstream effect of the PowerShell escaping issue but the 'live accessibility tree' wording is independently wrong.

sections.label: Code Pointer
sections.body: cli/browser4-cli/src/ (htmlsnapshot get empty-result error/hint text)

sections.label: AI Suggested Improvement
sections.body:
- Replace the 'live accessibility tree' wording with accurate guidance: verify the selector with htmlsnapshot grep, or re-capture with htmlsnapshot
- Don't echo a truncated selector in the suggestion line; show the exact selector the CLI received
